get_emeter.description: Read the energy meter's instantaneous readings. Metering models only (HS110, KP115) — a plug with no metering hardware answers with an error rather than a reading, so a consumer should decide from get_sysinfo's `feature`/`model` (see device.variants) whether to poll this at all. This is the state poll for the four emeter sensor entities below.

returns.description: Mains voltage in V (float). Current firmware. Absent on HS110 hardware v1, which sends `voltage_mv` instead.
returns.name: voltage

returns.description: Load current in A (float). Current firmware; see `current_ma`.
returns.name: current

returns.description: Instantaneous load power in W (float). Current firmware; see `power_mw`.
returns.name: power

returns.description: Accumulated consumption in kWh (float). Current firmware; see `total_wh`.
returns.name: total

returns.description: The HS110 hardware v1 spelling of `voltage`: millivolts. Divide by 1000 for V. Present INSTEAD OF `voltage`, not alongside it — this is the same normalization python-kasa's EmeterStatus performs, and both code paths exist in the vendor app (see evidence).
returns.name: voltage_mv

returns.description: HS110 hw v1 spelling of `current`: milliamperes. Divide by 1000 for A.
returns.name: current_ma

returns.description: HS110 hw v1 spelling of `power`: milliwatts. Divide by 1000 for W.
returns.name: power_mw

returns.description: HS110 hw v1 spelling of `total`: watt-hours. Divide by 1000 for kWh.
returns.name: total_wh

returns.description: 0 = no error, present on every method reply in this protocol. A non-zero code is what a plug with no metering hardware answers this command with.
returns.name: err_code

get_sysinfo.description: Read device info and current relay state. This is both the state poll (relay_state 0/1) and the discovery probe.

returns.description: 0 = off, 1 = on. The switch entity reads this.
returns.name: relay_state

returns.description: Hardware model with a region suffix, e.g. HS100(US). Match it against a `device.variants` entry's `model_prefix` as a PREFIX — the suffix varies by region and hardware revision.
returns.name: model

returns.description: Colon-separated capability list the device states about itself: "TIM" on a relay-only plug, "TIM:ENE" on a metering one. "ENE" is the runtime test for whether the emeter module — and therefore the four sensor entities — exist on this unit, and it is the check python-kasa's has_emeter makes. Prefer it over the model table when the reply carries it.
returns.name: feature

light_off.description: Turn a Kasa smart bulb off.

light_on.description: Turn a Kasa smart bulb on.

relay_off.description: Open the relay — turn the outlet off.

relay_off_child.description: Open one outlet's relay on a power strip. See relay_on_child.

child_id.description: The strip's own id for the outlet; see relay_on_child.

relay_on.description: Close the relay — turn the outlet on.

relay_on_child.description: Close one outlet's relay on a power strip — the same set_relay_state, scoped to a single child by its id via the context.child_ids envelope.

child_id.description: The strip's own id for the outlet (deviceId + 2-digit outlet index), from get_sysinfo's children[].id.

set_brightness.description: Set a Kasa smart bulb's brightness (1-100), switching it on.

strip_brightness.description: Set a Kasa light strip's brightness (1-100), switching it on.

strip_off.description: Turn a Kasa light strip off.

strip_on.description: Turn a Kasa light strip on.

device.name: TP-Link Kasa Smart Plug
device.notes:
The Kasa-era TP-Link smart plugs — HS100 and HS110 (HS110 adds energy monitoring), plus the same-protocol HS103/HS105 and KP105/KP115 (KP115 meters too; see device.variants for which models have the hardware, since that is the one difference that changes the entity surface) — speak a plaintext local protocol on TCP port 9999: JSON commands wrapped in a trivial XOR "autokey" cipher (initial key 0xAB), with no authentication of any kind. softScheck reverse-engineered it in 2016 and python-kasa (which backs Home Assistant's `tplink` integration, iot_class local_polling) has implemented it ever since. Day-to-day control is 100% LAN — block the plug from the internet at the router and everything here still works.
TP-Link the company is alive, so manufacturer_status is `active`; what is endangered is this local protocol. HS100 hardware v4 on firmware 1.1.0 (~2020) CLOSED port 9999 ("enhanced total encryption"), and newer hardware (EP25, KP125M, the whole Tapo line) moved to the encrypted KLAP/AES protocol with cloud-tied credentials — out of scope for this spec. Keep a working unit offline from vendor firmware updates to preserve the API.
SAFETY: the relay is mains-rated (13–16 A depending on region) and the protocol has NO authentication, so anything on the LAN can toggle the load. Segment the device accordingly.
This spec is transcribed from softScheck's write-up and python-kasa; the on-the-wire cipher and command vectors below are reproduced by scripts/test_kasa_spec.py from the YAML alone, but nothing here has been replayed against hardware by this project (verification: reported).

openness.notes: python-kasa is the authoritative implementation and is far better tested against hardware than this document; a consumer wanting a supported client should use it. This spec exists to document the protocol, not to compete with that library.

upstream_docs.covers: The port-9999 XOR-autokey cipher, the TCP length framing, and the system/emeter/netif JSON command tree.
upstream_docs.title: softScheck — Reverse Engineering the TP-Link HS110

credentials.notes: netif.set_stainfo carries the passphrase inside the same XOR-autokey obfuscation the rest of the protocol uses — that is not encryption, so the passphrase is effectively plaintext and the open setup AP is the only transport protection during provisioning. Post-setup control is unauthenticated: anything that can reach port 9999 can drive the plug.

factory_reset.effect: Clears Wi-Fi credentials, the device alias and any schedules/rules, returning the plug to its unprovisioned, AP-hosting state.

procedures.indicator: The status LED blinks amber/green rapidly to confirm the reset.
procedures.name: Press and hold the button (~5 seconds)

steps.action: With the plug powered, press and hold its physical button for about 5 seconds until the LED blinks rapidly, then release.
steps.notes: On models with a dedicated reset pinhole (some KP-series), hold that instead. A short press just toggles the relay.

methods.description: Join the plug's own `TP-LINK_Smart Plug_XXXX` AP and drive the port-9999 TCP-JSON protocol on it (the AP transport is the same protocol as normal control, not literal HTTP). Confirm the device answers get_sysinfo, then send netif.set_stainfo with the home network credentials; the plug drops its AP and joins.

steps.action: Factory reset the plug (or power a new one) and wait for its setup AP.
steps.expect: An open AP named `TP-LINK_Smart Plug_XXXX` appears.

steps.action: Join the setup AP from the provisioning client.
steps.expect: The client gets an address on the plug's setup subnet.

steps.action: Confirm the plug answers on the setup network.
steps.expect: A sysinfo reply carrying the plug's model, mac and deviceId.
The plug acknowledges, drops its AP and joins the home Wi-Fi.

steps.action: Rediscover the plug on the home network.
steps.expect: The plug answers a get_sysinfo broadcast on the home LAN.

setup.notes: A factory-fresh or reset plug hosts an open AP named `TP-LINK_Smart Plug_XXXX` and speaks the same port-9999 protocol on it. Joining it to the home Wi-Fi needs no cloud account: send `netif.set_stainfo` with the target SSID, passphrase and key type over the local protocol (this is what `kasa wifi join` does in python-kasa; the official Kasa app can also do it without signing in). The exact set_stainfo payload has not been replayed by this project, so confidence is low.

rejoin.notes: There is no documented in-place credential update over the local protocol; treat a router change as a factory reset and reprovision.

testing.notes: Read path verified live 2026-08-14 against a real HS210 3-way switch (alias placeholdered as "3-Way Switch", mac 00:31:92:AA:BB:CC), driving the protocol exactly as documented in kasa_protocol below. UDP discovery: the XOR-autokey get_sysinfo broadcast to 255.255.255.255:9999 (no length prefix) drew unauthenticated replies from EIGHT Kasa devices on the LAN across five model families — KP200, HS210, HS300, KL430, EP40 — each decoding to a valid sysinfo with model/alias/sw_ver. TCP control channel: a get_sysinfo to port 9999 with the documented 4-byte big-endian length prefix + XOR-autokey body returned the full sysinfo (model HS210(US), dev_name "Smart Wi-Fi 3-Way Light Switch", relay_state 0, rssi -59) with no authentication — confirming the length framing, the 0xAB running-key cipher (encrypt and decrypt directions) and the no-auth property together. These KP200/EP40/KL430 builds (2024-2025 firmware) still answer plaintext 9999, so the KP125M-era port closure is not universal. Not exercised: any state-changing write (system.set_relay_state and friends) — the switch controls real lighting and nobody authorized a toggle. The Smart Bulb / Light Strip variant state_probes and the two variant-scoped light entities' bindings are likewise unexercised against hardware (the strip's commands themselves were verified on a KL430; the probe and the entity state paths were not).

variants.notes: The original plug: relay only, no metering hardware — get_emeter answers with an error. Hardware v4 on firmware 1.1.0 (~2020) closed port 9999 entirely; such a unit speaks none of this spec.
Slim relay-only plug. No metering hardware.
Mini relay-only plug. No metering hardware.

The metering plug this spec's emeter surface exists for: HS100 plus an energy meter. Two field families are in the field — hardware v1 reports the emeter reply in milli-units (voltage_mv/current_ma/power_mw/total_wh) while later hardware reports plain SI floats, so the sensors below bind both (see their state_mapping `value_fallback`).
Slim relay-only plug, Kasa-protocol generation. No metering hardware.

Slim plug WITH energy monitoring — the KP-generation counterpart of the HS110, and the other model the emeter sensors apply to. Reports the plain SI float family; the milli-unit fallback is HS110 hw v1 only. Vendor-documented capability, not replayed against hardware by this project.

Kasa smart bulbs (KL110/KL130 …): same transport/cipher/framing, but switching and dimming go through the lightingservice's transition_light_state (light_on / light_off / set_brightness), and state lives in get_sysinfo.light_state. `keys_absent: length` is what separates a bulb from a light strip, which a bulb call is silently ignored by.

Kasa light strips (KL400/KL430): smartbulb-class, but driven through smartlife.iot.lightStrip.set_light_state (strip_on / strip_off / strip_brightness) — the bulb's lightingservice call is silently ignored. `length` (LED count) in get_sysinfo is the field that marks a strip; the strip commands were verified on a KL430.

The single-outlet relay family (every HS1xx/KP1xx above): a top-level relay_state and no children array. The plain Outlet switch applies here and nowhere else — a bulb ignores set_relay_state and a strip switches per child.

The multi-outlet family (HS300, KP200, KP303, EP40): outlets arrive as a `children` array, each switched by scoping the write with context.child_ids. The instanced Outlets entity applies here; the plain Outlet switch has no top-level relay_state to read on these.

The energy-metering members of the plug family (HS110, KP115 …), identified the way the model table's own comment recommends: the device's `feature` capability list carries "ENE" exactly when it has the emeter module. The four emeter sensors scope here, so a plug without a meter never draws four tiles that never fill.

entities.name: Voltage
entities.notes: Metering models only. `voltage` (volts) on current firmware; HS110 hw v1 sends `voltage_mv` (millivolts) instead — the value_fallback path, times its scale, is that reading in V.

entities.name: Current
entities.notes: Metering models only. `current` (amperes) on current firmware; HS110 hw v1 sends `current_ma` (milliamperes) instead.

entities.name: Power
entities.notes: Metering models only. `power` (watts) on current firmware; HS110 hw v1 sends `power_mw` (milliwatts) instead.

entities.name: Total Consumption
entities.notes: Metering models only. `total` (kWh) on current firmware; HS110 hw v1 sends `total_wh` (watt-hours) instead.

entities.name: Bulb
entities.notes: Kasa smart bulb (KL1xx): lightingservice.transition_light_state does the switching and dimming. Brightness is 1-100, the same range get_sysinfo.light_state.brightness reports.

entities.name: Light Strip
entities.notes: Kasa light strip (KL4xx): smartlife.iot.lightStrip.set_light_state does the switching and dimming (verified on a KL430); the bulb-class call is silently ignored on a strip. Brightness is 1-100.

app_static_analysis.confidence_notes: Derived from app code, not replayed against plug hardware; python-kasa's hardware-tested EmeterStatus agrees with both code paths.
confirms: The app builds an emeter request as an emeter module carrying an empty get_realtime method object — the request shape the get_emeter command's body documents.

The get_realtime reply is modelled with BOTH field families: voltage/current/power/total as floats and voltage_mv/current_ma/power_mw/total_wh as integers — the two hardware behaviours python-kasa's EmeterStatus normalizes between.

The app's milli-unit code path divides voltage_mv/current_ma/power_mw/total_wh by 1000 to reach V/A/W/kWh, while the legacy path reads the plain float fields directly — so the plain fields already carry SI units, as the entity units below claim.
app_static_analysis.source: TP-Link Kasa Android app 3.4.602 (com.tplink.kasa_android, APKPure xapk), jadx decompile (clean-room audit; derived facts only)

http_endpoints.description: Placeholder only. There is no HTTP surface: control is JSON over a raw TCP socket on port 9999 (see tplink_smarthome_protocol), not REST.
http_endpoints.name: Local API Placeholder

cipher.description: Byte-wise XOR with a running key. To ENCRYPT: start key = 0xAB (171); for each plaintext byte p, emit c = key XOR p, then set key = c. To DECRYPT: start key = 0xAB; for each ciphertext byte c, emit p = key XOR c, then set key = c. The key is thus the previous CIPHERTEXT byte after the first. This is obfuscation, not security — it has no secret.
cipher.name: XOR autokey

test_vectors.description: Reproducible with the algorithm above and nothing else; asserted by scripts/test_kasa_spec.py. Bytes are hex. The tiny inputs pin the cipher direction; the get_sysinfo vector is the canonical discovery datagram softScheck and python-kasa both publish.

command_tree.emeter.get_realtime: Metering models only (HS110, KP115) — instantaneous voltage/current/power/total. Bound as the get_emeter command and the four sensor entities below; see device.variants for which models have the hardware.
command_tree.netif.set_stainfo: Provisioning: join the plug to a Wi-Fi network (see device.setup).
command_tree.system.get_sysinfo: Device info + current relay_state. The state poll and the discovery probe.
command_tree.system.set_relay_state: Set the outlet relay: {state: 1} on, {state: 0} off.

discovery.response: Each Kasa-protocol device answers with a unicast datagram carrying the full get_sysinfo object (see the get_sysinfo command's returns): alias, model, deviceId, hwId, mac, rssi and relay_state. deviceId is the stable identity; alias is the user-facing name.

framing.tcp: Each message on the TCP stream is a 4-byte big-endian length prefix (the count of encrypted payload bytes, NOT including the prefix) followed by the XOR-encrypted JSON. The reply uses the same framing.
framing.udp: Discovery and its replies are a single datagram of the XOR-encrypted JSON with NO length prefix.

tplink_smarthome_protocol.multi_outlet_note: Power strips (HS300 / KP200 / KP303 / EP40) report a `children` array in get_sysinfo and address each outlet by wrapping a command in {"context":{"child_ids":["<deviceId>0N"]}}. Handled here now: the instanced "Outlets" switch enumerates the children, and relay_on_child / relay_off_child scope the write. A single-relay plug reports no `children`, so the plain "Outlet" switch covers it.
